newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen up on carry-over, peso soft.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen up on carry-over, peso soft.

text.p: Traders saw stocks opening on the upside Monday on momentum carried over from Friday and on forecasts that the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting would raise U.S. rates by no more than 25 basis points, leaving Mexican equities relatively unscathed.
"The market feels strong, we're seeing foreign investor interest once again," one desk trader said.
Traders expected the peso to open weak to sideways on an uncertain outlook for domestic interest rate movements at Tuesday's primary Cetes auction.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.9200/7.9500 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9260/7.9310 per dollar, compared to Friday's close of 7.9250/7.9290.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen relatively unchanged from Friday's high close of 19.25 percent with dealers hedging against possible strong U.S. retail data due on Tuesday.
